title: Responsible service and the law
lead: Michigan’s rules on ID, intoxication, liability, hours and training, and how the bar lives by them.

keyPoints.line: the ID has to prove it.
a real-looking Michigan license or state ID is a defense.
may serve only with training and an adult supervisor on shift.

read.bigIdea: 21 or older, proved by a real ID.
read.where: Selling or furnishing alcohol to a **minor** breaks the law and can make the bar **liable**. Under the Code, showing that the guest presented a **genuine-looking Michigan driver’s license or state ID** proving they were **21 or older** is a defense. Check **every** guest who might be under 30 (our house rule; GM to confirm). On staff: a **17-year-old** may serve at an on-premises licensee only after **server training** and with **adult supervisory staff** on shift.
read.mixup: An ID that’s expired or doesn’t look genuine doesn’t protect anyone. **When in doubt, don’t serve.**
read.sayIt: Could I see your ID, please? We check everyone.

keyPoints.line: by an intoxicated guest on our premises.
to eat, get help, or wait for a ride.

read.bigIdea: No sale, no drink, and get them home safe.
read.where: The Code says we may not **sell, serve or furnish** alcohol to someone who is **intoxicated**, and may not let an intoxicated person **drink** on the premises. We may not let them **loiter** either, but they **may stay** to **eat**, get **medical help**, or arrange a ride that isn’t them **driving**. And no one on staff may be **intoxicated** at work.
read.mixup: Cutting someone off isn’t throwing them out. They can stay to **eat** or wait for a **ride**.
read.sayIt: I can’t pour you another tonight, but I’d love to get you some food and water.

keyPoints.line: the person harmed and their family.
licensee to serve is presumed the one responsible.

read.bigIdea: Serving the wrong guest can cost the bar a lawsuit.
read.where: Michigan’s **dram shop** law (MCL 436.1801) lets a person **harmed** by a minor or a visibly intoxicated person, and their **family**, sue the licensee that **unlawfully sold** them alcohol, if that sale was a cause of the harm. Licensees other than the **last** one to serve the person are **presumed** not liable. The **intoxicated person** can’t sue under it. Claims must be filed within **2 years**, with written notice within **120 days** of hiring a lawyer.

stops.name: The guest
stops.text: Can’t sue under the dram shop law.

stops.name: The bar
stops.text: The **last** to serve is the one presumed responsible.

read.mixup: The last bar to serve isn’t automatically liable, but the law **presumes** the others aren’t. Don’t be the last pour to someone who’s had enough.

keyPoints.line: a.m.: no alcohol sold or served.
7 a.m. to noon needs a permit.
supervisors on every shift, where required.

read.bigIdea: Know the hours, keep the proof, train the team.
read.where: No alcohol may be **sold, given or furnished** between **2 a.m. and 7 a.m.** on any day; selling between **7 a.m. and noon on Sunday** takes a **permit**, and local rules can limit Sunday more. For on-premises licenses issued since the state’s **mandatory server training** began (and others the Commission names), a **trained supervisor** has to be on the premises **every shift** while alcohol is served, with **proof of training** kept on site. Log every **refusal** and **incident** the night it happens (house practice).
read.mixup: Last call isn’t 2 a.m. **2 a.m.** is when the selling has to have **stopped**.

sources: Michigan Liquor Control Code, MCL 436.1707 (legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-436-1707); Michigan Liquor Control Code, MCL 436.1801 (legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-436-1801); Michigan Liquor Control Code, MCL 436.1906 (legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-436-1906); Michigan Liquor Control Code, MCL 436.2114 (legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-436-2114); House practice (ours; GM to confirm). Written for Mise in our own words, Nov 12, 2026.
